source_refs.note: Topic 7.3.3 with the Did You Know and class activity (PDF 184-185, printed 181-182). Long question 2 is answered; the activity answer is illustrative, flagged.

items: Government initiatives: build internet infrastructure where it is missing; in Pakistan the Universal Service Fund (USF) takes internet services to villages and remote areas.
Educational programmes: schools and community centres teach people to use computers and the internet for study and daily tasks.
Public-private partnerships: government working with businesses and non-profits can make technology more affordable.

blocks.text: The book notes that the Government of Pakistan has launched initiatives such as mobile broadband in remote regions, but many areas still lack reliable connectivity (Did You Know).

blocks.prompt: Explain bridging the digital divide and the role of government initiatives, with examples from Pakistan (long question 2).
blocks.explanation: Bridging the divide means giving everyone fair access to devices, connectivity and skills so all have the same chances to learn, work and take part. Government has a central role because it can fund infrastructure where companies see little profit: the Universal Service Fund extends internet to villages and remote areas, and mobile broadband projects reach rural regions. Government can also support digital literacy in schools and partner with businesses and non-profits to make devices and data cheaper. Gaps remain, so these efforts must continue.

blocks.prompt: Class activity: write a short paragraph on how your school or community can help bridge the digital divide.
blocks.explanation: For example: the school computer lab could open on weekends for parents and neighbours, older students could teach basic phone and internet skills, and old devices could be repaired and donated to families without them.

items: Bridge the divide with infrastructure (USF), digital literacy and public-private partnerships.
